name: Bielsismo
scopeNote: Bielsismo (also 'bielsista' in Wilson/SI and FourFourTwo) as the idea: high, man-oriented pressing over the whole pitch (Grantland: 'Man-mark and press the hell out of your opponent'), immediate counter-pressing, vertical and fast attacks with wide forwards and wing-backs, a spare centre-back against the opponent's strikers, intense repetitive training, and a 3-3-1-3 / 4-3-3 / 4-1-4-1 structure that shifts with the number of opposing strikers. Period 1990 (Newell's Old Boys title under Bielsa) to 2020 (Leeds Championship title and the La Nacion Bielsa-Guardiola piece); profilePeriod start 1990 and end 2020 are year-only (partial) because exact start of Bielsa's Newell's spell was not checked here. Bielsa's later Leeds Premier League seasons and Uruguay are outside the evidence. Popular label caution: '3-3-3-1' and '3-3-1-3' are tactical-notation shorthand; Grantland says formation notation does not fit (man-marking plus one free safety), and Sampaoli's Chile is better described by Spielverlagerung as 4-1-2-1-2 / 3-4-1-2 with man-marking elements. Universidad de Chile 2012 (Sampaoli) is the earliest evidence of the line outside Bielsa; the 2011 title spell itself was not covered by a page here.
openQuestions: Rigid vs adaptive: Bielsa says 'Yo no cedo mis ideas y Sampaoli sí' (2017) and 'the idea of having alternative plans is considered a virtue, but I do not agree' (Hay, FFT 2020); Sampaoli varied (4-3-3 to 3-3-1-3, back 3 or 2 depending on opposing strikers per Hardtackle; tempered pressing and used Aranguiz to isolate Messi in the 2015 final per SBS/SI). Treat flexibility as a Sampaoli difference, not part of the core idea.

Marking: Grantland (2015, Marseille) says Bielsa teams man-mark 'all over the field'; Hardtackle/Spielverlagerung describe Sampaoli's Chile as man-marking dropping players and pressing ball-orientated in the halfspaces ('ball-orientated press' when the ball is in the flank); Sampaoli himself says bielsismo 'en defensa hace el uno contra uno' (2024, outside period). Full-pitch man-marking is clearly documented for Bielsa, only partly for Sampaoli.

Midfield: Sky (Herrera 2013) says Bielsa used a classic enganche (Matias Fernandez) while Sampaoli used all-round midfielders (Vidal, Aranguiz, Gutierrez), and Spielverlagerung describes Sampaoli's Chile using a diamond with Valdivia and juego de posicion elements ('Posesion 74'), which is closer to Guardiola than to Bielsa's directness. Possession weight differs between exemplars.

Label origin: 'discipulo' (Bielsa denies it, 2017) and 'bielsista'/'bielsismo' appear in press (SI/Wilson 2015, FourFourTwo 2017). No Bielsa-coined label was found; Sampaoli uses 'bielsismo' versus 'guardiolismo' in 2024 (Marca via FutbolUy), outside the period and secondary. Earliest primary use of the label not located.

Fatigue claim: Grantland and SBS say Bielsa teams (Bilbao, Marseille, and Sampaoli's Sevilla) fade late in seasons; Hay's FFT says Leeds soft-tissue injuries were lower than average. Evidence on the physical cost is contested.

Exemplar ids: manager marcelo-bielsa and jorge-sampaoli and team chile-2015-16 are given by the brief; Sampaoli's Universidad de Chile 2010-12 was not given a catalog id here and rests on one 2012 interview (24horas).

sources.title: Copa America Preview: Chile
sources.evidence: Chile have been synonymous with a 3-at-the-back first with Bielsa, and now with Sampaoli. Sampaoli has used a 3-4-1-2 regularly with great success over the last couple of years however has employed a formation with two centre backs at times.

sources.title: Legacy of Bielsa
sources.evidence: "The tactics are similar except for some minor details," explains Herrera. "It can be a 4-1-2-3, 4-2-1-3 or 3-3-1-3. Bielsa used a classic 'enganche' which was almost always Matías Fernández, while Sampaoli prefers a mix of all-round midfielders such as Arturo Vidal, Aránguiz and Felipe Gutiérrez."

sources.title: A year with Marcelo Bielsa (Leeds 2018/19)
sources.evidence: he uses a 4-1-4-1 formation against teams with one striker, and 3-3-1-3 (a system that earned his 'El Loco' nickname at Newell's 30 years ago) when the opposition play with two up front. His players are coached to slip neatly between the two structures mid-game

sources.title: World Cup 2014: Tactics of Chile
sources.evidence: Against teams with two up front, Sampaoli favors a back three and against teams with one up front, Sampaoli favors fielding a pair of center backs. This way, Chile always have a spare man at the back, allowing them to mark and still have one player available to sweep behind.

sources.title: Sampaoli: Grababa a Bielsa en un cassette
sources.evidence: Los métodos de entrenamiento, un sistema madre que es 4-3-3 y un sistema de adaptación que, según cómo se pare el rival, puede ser 3-3-1-3.

sources.title: Grantland: Bielsa Burnout (Marseille v PSG)
sources.evidence: Allegedly, Marseille lined up in a 3-3-3-1 formation yesterday. That is an exceedingly odd and unrealistic setup of positions and responsibilities. [...] It's not complicated; it's just incompatible with traditional tactical notation.

sources.title: Copa America Preview: Chile
sources.evidence: Chile build up from very deep, drawing out the opposition. The centre-backs spread to the corners of the 18-yard area to make them more difficult to press as play is stretched over a wider area.

sources.title: Training Ground Guru: Bielsa tactics and philosophy
sources.evidence: A player like Gary Medel sees the 2 v 1 when playing out from the back in a way that the more natural central defenders don't. That for me is why Bielsa saw value in playing him deeper in the build-up play as a central defender instead of in his more natural position of centre midfield.

sources.title: Las 10 coincidencias tácticas entre los equipos de Bielsa y Guardiola
sources.evidence: ambos arrancan desde el principio, tratando de tener un arquero que, además de tratar de atajar las pelotas que van en dirección al arco, tengan una buena técnica con los pies. Tanto Bielsa como Guardiola suelen entrenar más de 20 formas distintas para salir desde el fondo

sources.title: Chile - Bolivia 5:0
sources.evidence: Sampaoli's Chile emerged as unsurprising victors against Bolivia whose uncoordinated pressing system was exposed by the intelligent hosts' possession game.

sources.title: Chile-Argentina Copa America final (SI)
sources.evidence: Sampaoli has tempered the pressing a little anyway in this tournament, seemingly to acknowledge that many of his players are weary and could not maintain such intensity over a full tournament. The approach has been more possession-based

sources.title: Las 10 coincidencias tácticas entre los equipos de Bielsa y Guardiola
sources.evidence: para Bielsa, es un avance respaldado hasta con siete jugadores en el área rival y resuelto con una asistencia de centro atrás en el menor tiempo posible.

sources.title: Grantland: Bielsa Burnout
sources.evidence: Bielsa's game plans are built on an exceedingly simple premise: Man-mark and press the hell out of your opponent. [...] it's not at all unusual to witness six or seven Bielsa pawns flying into the opposition's end immediately after losing the ball.

sources.title: Copa America Preview: Chile
sources.evidence: Chile do most of their defending in the opposition's half and their aggressive pressing and counterpressing is what has made them such a footballing cult. They are always looking to win the ball instead of just dropping off

sources.title: Copa America Preview: Chile
sources.evidence: Chile set up a high press with the man on the ball almost always being pressed, usually by the ever-energetic Sanchez. Their back five allows them to man-mark men dropping to receive the ball from their defenders without leaving too much space in behind.

sources.title: World Cup 2014: Tactics of Chile
sources.evidence: Chile play a high-energy game with a high line and a high press. [...] If the keeper has the ball, the center forward looks to close him down; the wide forwards mark the center backs; the wingbacks push up to deny passing lanes to the fullbacks

sources.title: Explaining Marcelo Bielsa (FourFourTwo)
sources.evidence: So determined was Bielsa to implement that strategy, he instructed keeper Norberto Scoponi to intentionally hit goal-kicks out of play for a throw-in, reasoning that the midfield could win the ball back quickly and create an artificial turnover. Newell's became a pressing machine.

sources.title: Grantland: Bielsa Burnout
sources.evidence: Like every Bielsa team since the beginning of time, Marseille man-mark all over the field. [...] A set back three or four that does things like defend space, pressure and cover as a unit, or play an offside trap simply doesn't exist for Bielsa. Instead, there's just one guy acting as a free safety while everybody else mans up.

sources.title: Chile-Argentina Copa America final (SI)
sources.evidence: The suggestion is that Sampaoli will switch to a back three, with Marcelo Diaz dropping in at sweeper and Francisco Silva coming in for Jose Rojas to act as a man-marker.

sources.title: Chile - Bolivia 5:0
sources.evidence: The pressing system of Chile was very flexible in the positioning of the individual players but was overall a 4-3-3-turned-4-1-4-1 shape.

sources.title: Training Ground Guru: Bielsa tactics and philosophy
sources.evidence: In order to achieve the playing style and philosophy outlined above, Bielsa started doing something simple, yet counter-intuitive: using midfielders in the defensive line. For Chile, Gary Medel, who had played as a midfielder throughout his career and gained the nickname 'Pitbull', moved back into the centre of defence.

sources.title: Legacy of Bielsa
sources.evidence: An excellent passing game coupled with rapid transitions from defence to attack was fused with an aggressive pressing style that saw the team work tirelessly to win the ball back.

sources.title: World Cup 2014: Tactics of Chile
sources.evidence: When Chile do win the ball back, high up the pitch, they transition quickly and look to have as many men running beyond the ball as possible. [...] allowing Chile to have up to six men running in on goal.

sources.title: Why Sampaoli is Barcelona's number one target
sources.evidence: An obvious risk of the Bielsa/Sampaoli model of play is the space that it can leave the opposition to launch counter-attacks. Bielsa had seemed inflexible on this point, but Sampaoli had been studying how to make a subtle alteration to the balance of his side.

sources.title: Copa America Preview: Chile
sources.evidence: Chile always try to stretch the opposition both laterally and vertically. They stretch the opposition laterally when they have the ball in the opposition's half using the high and wide positioning of the fullbacks.

sources.title: Why Sampaoli is Barcelona's number one target
sources.evidence: throwing both full backs forward at the same time to create two-against-one situations high up the pitch and playing at high tempo with furious energy.

sources.title: A year with Marcelo Bielsa (Leeds 2018/19)
sources.evidence: His players are coached to slip neatly between the two structures mid-game, overloading the wings and using interplay in congested areas to get through the wall of defenders in front of them.

sources.title: Las 10 coincidencias tácticas entre los equipos de Bielsa y Guardiola
sources.evidence: Bielsa marca hombre a hombre en las pelotas paradas; Pep hace zona. [...] Bielsa entiende que debe haber responsabilidades individuales, que cuando cae el centro nadie se pregunte "¿es mío o tuyo?".

sources.title: Las 10 coincidencias tácticas entre los equipos de Bielsa y Guardiola
sources.evidence: En las prácticas, le lanzamos 220 centros a un tipo, buscando que hombre y pelota se encuentren en un punto exacto. Así se hacen goles con pelota parada. (Bielsa, en el libro "Los 11 caminos al gol")

sources.title: A year with Marcelo Bielsa (Leeds 2018/19)
sources.evidence: The idea of having alternative plans is considered a virtue, but I do not agree with this point of view [...] Bielsa held a 66-minute briefing at Thorp Arch to detail his pre-match analysis in full

sources.title: Las 10 coincidencias tácticas entre los equipos de Bielsa y Guardiola
sources.evidence: Bielsa (por lo general) casi nunca haría un cambio defensivo para sostener un resultado. El Loco prefiere morir con la suya que perder con otro estilo

sources.title: Sampaoli: Grababa a Bielsa en un cassette
sources.evidence: Estamos mirando todos los partidos de Boca de local. [...] Sacamos jugadas, editamos situaciones que tienen que ver con cómo defienden en un sector u otro de la cancha, cómo atacan, las transiciones, las pelotas paradas.

sources.title: Grantland: Bielsa Burnout
sources.evidence: Beyond the swirling, hornet's-nest pressing [...] Only four of their 17 shots came in the last half hour. [...] Marseille looked completely spent.

sources.title: Chile-Argentina Copa America final (SI)
sources.evidence: Sampaoli, although far more classically bielsista than Martino, may himself be forced to move away form the hard-pressing game he has traditionally favored.

sources.title: Sampaoli: Grababa a Bielsa en un cassette
sources.evidence: La presión constante, la recuperación inmediata, no tener temores por más que juguemos contra equipos con mayores presupuestos, no pensar en defendernos y no resignar la posibilidad de atacar, que la rebeldía sea un rasgo

sources.title: Legacy of Bielsa
sources.evidence: "I've got different characteristics. I think that Marcelo is among the leading coaches in the history of world football. So, making comparisons or thinking that someone is similar is unfair [...]" (Sampaoli to FIFA)

sources.title: Bielsa: Sampaoli no es discípulo mío
sources.evidence: Una de las virtudes de los entrenadores es la flexibilidad. Yo no cedo mis ideas y Sampaoli sí porque tiene un poder de adaptación que yo no tengo

sources.title: Explaining Marcelo Bielsa (FourFourTwo)
sources.evidence: "A lot of coaches will tell you that you must decide your philosophy based on the players you've got – I don't agree," he once said. [...] "I'm an extremist," he added. "I manage according to how I feel. I don't compromise"

sources.title: Training Ground Guru: Bielsa tactics and philosophy
sources.evidence: Bielsa has said "movement, rotation, concentration and improvisation" are the four cornerstones of his footballing philosophy.

sources.title: Training Ground Guru: Bielsa tactics and philosophy
sources.evidence: Perhaps the finest example of all is Javi Martinez, who had played as a goalscoring midfielder before Bielsa took over at Bilbao. The Argentine turned him into a magnificent central defender

sources.title: Grantland: Bielsa Burnout
sources.evidence: When Bielsa was at Athletic Bilbao, Guardiola described his team as such: "They all run up … and they all run down again. Up, down, up, down, up, down. They're fascinating." It's a great approach — as long as the players buy in.

sources.title: Copa America Preview: Chile
sources.evidence: Chile are also extremely fortunate that they have a goalkeeper who is very comfortable on the ball under pressure and is arguably the best 'keeper at passing in the world.

sources.title: Legacy of Bielsa
sources.evidence: Sampaoli has also brought in players Bielsa never considered integral to his squad, such as José Rojas and Marcelo Díaz.

sources.title: A year with Marcelo Bielsa (Leeds 2018/19)
sources.evidence: Bielsa chose to run with a small group by the standards of the Championship, using fewer than 20 senior professionals and asking the academy to plug any gaps. Seven under-23s have made first-team bows this season [...] "When a team wins regularly, no one is tired,"

sources.title: Explaining Marcelo Bielsa (FourFourTwo)
sources.evidence: Bielsa's personally-scouted stream of young, hungry players with fire in their bellies turning Newell's Old Boys into one of Argentina's most promising sides.

sources.title: Why Sampaoli is Barcelona's number one target
sources.evidence: Between 2007-10, Bielsa had groomed an impressive generation of young Chilean players, successfully transmitted his philosophy and attacking mentality, and given Chilean football the identity it had always lacked.

sources.title: A year with Marcelo Bielsa (Leeds 2018/19)
sources.evidence: "I love my players," he said, "but if they were close to me then they would respect me less because they would see how I really am" [...] He runs them into the ground, applies heavy amounts of tactical repetition and uses a large backroom team to coach players individually.

sources.title: Explaining Marcelo Bielsa (FourFourTwo)
sources.evidence: He began to set the squad's younger players homework. They were to buy El Grafico, Solo Futbol and Clarin, and research how upcoming opposition played [...] Their findings would then be presented to the squad and a training session built around them.

sources.title: Explaining Marcelo Bielsa (FourFourTwo)
sources.evidence: "There are two types of street fighters," declared Bielsa, entering a nervous dressing room with powerful certainty. [...] Argentina won 3-1.

sources.title: A year with Marcelo Bielsa (Leeds 2018/19)
sources.evidence: Every Wednesday, 45 minutes are set aside for a 'murderball' session: 11 vs 11 with no free-kicks and the ball in play constantly.

statedView.quote: Una de las virtudes de los entrenadores es la flexibilidad. Yo no cedo mis ideas y Sampaoli sí porque tiene un poder de adaptación que yo no tengo
statedView.speaker: Marcelo Bielsa
statedView.note: Reported by agency from a congress in Rio; also: Sampaoli no es discípulo mío (label rejected).

statedView.quote: Los métodos de entrenamiento, un sistema madre que es 4-3-3 y un sistema de adaptación que, según cómo se pare el rival, puede ser 3-3-1-3. La presión constante, la recuperación inmediata, no tener temores [...] no pensar en defendernos y no resignar la posibilidad de atacar, que la rebeldía sea un rasgo
statedView.speaker: Jorge Sampaoli
statedView.note: Interview with 24horas.cl about what he took from Bielsa; Universidad de Chile.

statedView.quote: The most important thing was picking up from where Marcelo Bielsa had left off in the previous qualifying campaign
statedView.speaker: Jorge Sampaoli
statedView.note: Told to FIFA, as reported by Sky Sports in 2014; exact FIFA date not located.

statedView.speaker: Marcelo Bielsa
statedView.note: Four cornerstones, per Training Ground Guru; no original source found.

statedView.quote: A lot of coaches will tell you that you must decide your philosophy based on the players you've got – I don't agree
statedView.speaker: Marcelo Bielsa

statedView.quote: Running is commitment, running is understanding, running is everything.
statedView.speaker: Marcelo Bielsa
statedView.note: Grantland 2015: 'As he's said in the past'.

statedView.quote: El 'Bielsismo' es más directo y en defensa hace el uno contra uno. Antes era muy bielsista y ahora más Guardiolista
statedView.speaker: Jorge Sampaoli
statedView.note: Marca interview via FutbolUy; outside period, shows the label from a manager.

influences: Cruyff-Guardiola (Guardiola cites Bielsa: 'Eso lo aprendí de Bielsa', La Nacion)

exemplars.reason: Originator: Newell's 1990, Chile 2007-11, Bilbao, Marseille, Leeds; man-marking all over the pitch, 3-3-1-3.
Self-declared follower (Universidad de Chile 2012, Chile 2012-16); adapted the model with variations and more flexibility.
Copa America 2015 and Centenario 2016 winners; high pressing, 3-4-1-2 / 4-1-2-1-2, Bielsa legacy per Spielverlagerung.

confidence.reason: Several tier B sources agree for Chile 2014-15 and the core ideas, but Bielsa's own spells (Newell's, Bilbao, Marseille, Leeds) rest on tier C press; Universidad de Chile has one interview; many stated views are attributed only.
